claim: Preserving hypothesis-to-intervention-to-evidence-to-finding provenance enables better learning-system improvement than storing conversational summaries alone.
rationale: Structured provenance should make failed assumptions, contradictions, and reusable learning-policy evidence easier to inspect and improve.
falsification: The structured ledger does not materially improve later diagnosis, replication, or policy decisions compared with lightweight summaries, net of maintenance cost.
scope: Evaluate after enough sessions exist for retrospective comparison.
